feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical/strategic blend is compelling. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond scale metrics, and has a few style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scope: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, broad platform/tool expertise.  
- Professional, readable tone with a strong summary and relevant mix of strategy, operations, analytics, web, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements, not just responsibilities or scale: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption improvements, campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and avoid repetition.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; use the serial comma consistently (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); standardize punctuation in bullets and section formatting.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and relevant scope, but it reads generic in places and overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more directly to public-sector/advocacy digital leadership would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper phrase like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations, with a strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused communications. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and building the systems and workflows that support complex organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat Core Competencies/Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- The long channel list duplicates detail already covered in Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “CMS strategy, governance & administration.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow: strategy/governance, platforms/workflows, analytics, stakeholder communications, multimedia.
- Prioritize recent, role-aligned strengths from current and latest roles, such as CMS modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS strategy, governance & administration • Editorial workflows & content operations • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow systems & automation • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it only for broad themes not repeated elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Rephrase for outcomes, not duties: “Built modular Drupal campaign experiences and member toolkits” → “Delivered modular Drupal microsites and campaign toolkits that improved reuse, publishing speed, or campaign scalability” (add metrics if available).
- Make the AI search bullet the anchor achievement: specify scope, prototype/stage, content corpus, or expected user benefit.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy, governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize advisory/consulting scope and new initiatives instead.
- Microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget across enterprise platforms.”
- Combine and tighten web modernization: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add metrics for email/social growth, video output, cost savings from the in-house studio, reporting speed, or governance efficiency.
- Reduce generic phrasing like “strengthened” and “improving strategic decision-making”; use concrete verbs such as “standardized,” “centralized,” “launched,” or “cut.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and systems.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries; emphasize building the studio, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and relies on soft phrasing like “helped.” Make it more ownership-driven and distinct by emphasizing executional leadership before the later director-level strategy/governance work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, leading editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Tighten and combine overlapping bullets: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, growth in subscribers, reduced publishing turnaround, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial planning/coordination” and “publishing workflows” overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version focused on hands-on channel management and content production.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies and reads generic rather than differentiated. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “publishing standards” to better match recent leadership roles.
- Keep terms parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing broad strategy with tactical planning language.
- If space allows, add one stronger differentiator such as “high-volume public-sector communications” or “enterprise web modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo role bullets; keep this section as a concise summary, not a repeat.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript/jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-enabled search, since those are most supported by recent NACo work.
- Drop lower-priority platforms here unless central to target roles; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages in “Technical + IT” instead.
- Consider replacing “Airtable systems” with “operational workflow systems” if you want broader, more senior positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies; keep it in one place if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a generic tool list. Tighten it to emphasize decision-making, measurement, and optimization impact rather than repeating platforms already listed elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Analytics, Measurement & Optimization**
- Rewrite as: **GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • Analytics infrastructure and dashboarding • KPI and measurement framework design • Executive/leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis**
- Group tools first, then capabilities; this scans better and sounds more senior than a flat list.
- If space allows, replace one generic phrase with an outcome-oriented one, e.g. **decision-ready reporting** or **insight-driven optimization**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; consider keeping tools there and making this section more strategic/capability-led.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use distinct wording like **executive reporting and KPI frameworks**.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward outcomes and scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid overly technical fragments; “PTZ camera systems” works better as “PTZ/multi-camera production systems.”
- If space allows, align with recent experience by emphasizing studio buildout and event delivery, e.g. “Studio operations and livestream workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; vary wording here to avoid repetition.
- Specific tools belong in “Technical + IT,” so keep this section focused on capabilities, not software/hardware lists.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, credible platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first and de-emphasize lower-signal tools: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light proficiency/context instead of a raw list, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it was only used lightly; it reads less strategic than the rest and may dilute seniority.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use **Microsoft Power Pages** rather than just **Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or using this section for only platform-specific tools not named elsewhere.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint already appear in multiple places via experience and skills, so avoid repeating them without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior leader, this should emphasize implementation scope and modern tooling rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add level/context to avoid sounding entry-level: **Front-end implementation for Drupal/WordPress, tag deployment, lightweight serverless scripts, and deployment automation**
- If space allows, replace older/basic terms with outcome-oriented wording: **Custom front-end builds, third-party/API integrations, serverless edge scripting, release automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep detail in one place only.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure; consider moving it to **Data, Analytics & Optimization** if that section needs more depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more implementation-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems used for automation and operational coordination, not general collaboration tools.
- Suggested rewrite: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello**  
- If accurate, add light qualifiers for impact: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello (project and editorial workflow management)**
- Consider moving **Slack** and **Teams** to a separate “Collaboration Tools” line only if you need them for ATS coverage; otherwise cut for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same language here.
- Basecamp, Slack, and Teams feel lower-value versus the stronger automation/platform tools above.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this line is too generic and underplays your stronger, recent leadership in email operations. It should signal enterprise-scale platform ownership rather than read like a basic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Email & Engagement Systems:** Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If space allows, add scope: **Enterprise email platforms for newsletter, campaign and member communications**
- If these were hands-on in recent roles, consider: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations**
- Best upgrade: tie to scale elsewhere in the CV by reflecting outcomes in experience bullets, e.g., “managed email platforms supporting newsletters to tens of thousands of county officials”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about newsletters/email reach; avoid repeating audience-size claims here.
- Don’t add “social” or “campaigns” language if it duplicates broader channel leadership already covered in recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and concrete so it reads as the foundation for the leadership roles that follow.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize build-stage impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outputs: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or early-building that program.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; here, specify setup/implementation rather than ongoing leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the media work concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research projects that supported NACo program development and policy initiatives.”
- Tighten the media portion: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one concrete outcome: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, stakeholder groups served, or how content was used (member engagement, policy communications, events).
- Consider a one-line version to save space: “Coordinated innovation/research projects supporting NACo programs and policy work; produced digital content and launched the organization’s first podcast.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid overexplaining production tasks here.
- Podcast/video production themes recur elsewhere, so keep this item focused on being the first/launch role.
